tagline: Over the Berkshires on a road made for the automobile.
intro: Out of Lee, US 20 climbs east through Becket to its summit on Morey Hill at 1,775 feet, then comes down through Chester and along the Westfield River through Huntington to Russell. It was the first road over a mountain range built for the automobile, pushed for by Lee resident Cortland Bishop and opened in September 1910.

The opening was held at the top on a rainy day. Dignitaries and visiting motorists brought rocks from home and left them in a pile there, and the pile kept growing into the cairn that marks the summit.

moments.title: Morey Hill summit
moments.text: The cairn stands at the corner of Route 20 and Fred Snow Road, where antique cars gathered in 2010 to mark the road's hundredth year.

moments.title: Keystone Arches
moments.text: Stone railroad bridges of about 1840, laid up without mortar or steel and the first of their kind in the country, with a 2.5-mile trail out to them.

moments.title: Huntington
moments.text: The West Branch joins the Westfield River at the village, and to the north two villages, Knightville and Indian Hollow, were removed for the Knightville Dam between 1939 and 1941.
